verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {plaintiff_name}, son/daughter/wife of {plaintiff_father_name}, resident of {plaintiff_address}, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above plaint are true and correct to my personal knowledge, and matters of legal submission are believed true on advice of counsel. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Plaintiff

promptInstructions: Draft a plaint for ejectment / eviction of tenant under Transfer of Property Act, 1882 — applicable ONLY to premises NOT covered by state rent control legislation.

CRITICAL STEP-1: Verify rent control applicability. Each state has its own rent control act with thresholds, exemptions, and area coverage. Filing TPA suit for rent-controlled premises is FATAL — only rent controller has jurisdiction.

State rent control statutes to cross-check (illustrative): Delhi Rent Control Act 1958 (exemption: rent > Rs. 3,500/month + premises let to MNC/govt; large bungalows); Maharashtra Rent Control Act 1999 (exemption: rent > Rs. 25,000/month, certain non-residential, etc.); UP Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act 1972 (applies to urban areas, exemption for newly constructed for 40 years); Bihar Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act 1982; Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act 2017; West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act 1997. ALWAYS verify current statute for the specific state.
FOR LAWIE PROMPT: If user indicates premises is in rent-control-covered area/category, FLAG: 'Use rent control eviction petition before Rent Controller, not civil court TPA suit.'
Para 1-2: Parties.
Para 3: Premises description — full schedule with boundaries, address, nature (residential / commercial / agricultural). Annexed site plan recommended.
Para 4: Plaintiff's title — chain of title with source documents.
Para 5: Creation of tenancy — date, mode (oral / unregistered / registered lease — note S.107 TPA requires registered lease for terms > 1 year), monthly rent, security deposit, purpose.
Para 6: WHY rent control NOT applicable — premises exempted by rent / area / type / age etc., cite the specific exemption provision of the state act.

Para 7: Ground of eviction — choose appropriate: (a) Termination of month-to-month tenancy by 15-day notice u/s 106 TPA; (b) Expiry of fixed-term lease; (c) Forfeiture u/s 111(g) TPA on breach of express condition (with forfeiture clause); (d) Forfeiture on denial of landlord's title; (e) Determination by efflux of time u/s 111(a).

Para 8: Notice to quit u/s 106 TPA. POST-2003 AMENDMENT: notice is 15 days for all leases (residential/commercial) terminating with end of month of tenancy. For agricultural and manufacturing tenancies, 6 months ending with year of tenancy. Notice must be in writing, signed by landlord/agent, served by registered post or in person. PROVISO: notice no longer rendered invalid merely by procedural defects if substance and intent clear (S.106(3) — 2003 amendment).
Cite: Aero Traders v. Ravinder Kumar (2014) 9 SCC 153 — notice substantial compliance post-amendment.
Para 9: Plead tender / refusal of possession by tenant after notice expiry.
Para 10: Rent arrears (if any) and mesne profits — Order XX R.12 CPC — court may award mesne profits up to delivery of possession.
Para 11: Cause of action — date of expiry of notice / refusal.
Para 12: Limitation — Article 67 Limitation Act — 12 years from determination of tenancy.
Para 13: Jurisdiction — S.16 CPC where premises situate.
Para 14: Valuation and court fee — state Schedule (typically annual rent or 1.5x annual rent for ejectment).
Para 15: Prayer for: (i) ejectment; (ii) recovery of arrears; (iii) mesne profits; (iv) interest u/s 34; (v) costs.

Where lease is registered, suit can be filed in regular civil court. Where in Small Causes Courts area (Bombay/Calcutta/Madras/Hyderabad), Small Causes Court has exclusive jurisdiction for premises possession suits up to certain valuation.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

sections.description: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract — 15 days notice (post-2003 amendment); 6 months for agricultural/manufacturing

Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee

Determination of lease — (a) efflux of time; (b) specified event; (c) merger; (d) express surrender; (e) implied surrender; (f) forfeiture (denial of title / breach of express condition / insolvency); (g) notice to quit; (h) acquisition by Government
Relief against forfeiture for non-payment of rent
Decree for possession and mesne profits

filing_checklist: Affidavit in support of plaint (Order VI R.15(4))
Title documents — sale deed, mutation, parent deeds, property tax receipts
Lease deed (if written; if registered, certified copy)
Notice to quit u/s 106 TPA — original + postal receipt + AD card + tracking report
Affidavit confirming rent control act inapplicability with reasoning
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: plaintiff_name and defendant_name must not be empty
rent_control_applicability must be specified — non-applicability ground required
notice_under_s106 must not be empty (proof of valid notice essential)
notice_expiry_date must precede suit filing date
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
If state rent control applies, REJECT and flag for rent controller petition instead
key_citations: Aero Traders Pvt Ltd v. Ravinder Kumar Suri (2014) 9 SCC 153 — Substantial compliance with S.106 notice post-2003 amendment
Karnataka State Industrial Investment & Development Corp v. Cavalet India Ltd (2005) 4 SCC 456 — Notice to quit principles
Pradesh Kumar Bajpai v. Binod Behari Sarkar (1980) 3 SCC 11 — Forfeiture and waiver
Murli S. Deora v. Union of India (2001) 8 SCC 765 — Wrongly invoked in some eviction matters; verify state rent law
Vinod Kumar v. Surjit Kaur (2002) 4 SCC 207 — Validity of notice under S.106
Smt. Juthika Mulick v. Dr. Mahendra Yashwant Bal (2014) 11 SCC 174 — Tenancy at sufferance and mesne profits
Bhagabandhu Sahu v. Nilamani Tripathy (2014) — Distinction between rent control and TPA jurisdiction
